clearing_status.fact: On Feb 25, 2025 the SEC formally extended compliance dates by one year (90 FR 11134, eff. Mar 4 2025): cash from Dec 31 2025 to Dec 31 2026; repo from Jun 30 2026 to Jun 30 2027. As of Sep 22 2026, Acting Chair Uyeda stated at the 2026 U.S. Treasury Market Conference that 'the SEC does not currently intend to extend these deadlines' (sec.gov, Sept 22 2026). No second extension has been announced; the Dec 31 2026 cash deadline has not yet passed.
clearing_status.rationale: One official 12-month extension was formally granted (Feb 2025), satisfying the rubric's score-1 criterion of 'an official extension granted.' No second extension has been announced and the first deadline has not yet passed, so rubric score 2 is not triggered.

dissent.view: ICI submitted a letter to Acting Chair Uyeda in Feb 2025 requesting a further extension of at least 24 months (to at least Jun 30 2028) for Treasury repo clearing; if granted this would push to score 2, but SEC has publicly refused further extension as of Sep 2026.

TBAC (May 2026) noted 'it is possible that clearing will not be available to all participants in all regions by the deadline,' signaling readiness risk but stopping short of characterizing a second delay.

plan_financing.fact: 10y JGB auction on Oct 6 2026 cleared with bid-to-cover of 3.76 (MOF/Bloomberg, Oct 6 2026); 10y yield held ~3.02-3.12% in early October, up ~132bps YoY and ~10bps in the past month, near 30-year highs. Takaichi pledged in her Oct 5 Diet address that fiscal measures would be funded without new bond issuance, but Nomura economists noted the rhetoric 'does not necessarily mean policy will actually be adjusted.' Supplementary budget earlier in 2026 included new deficit bonds (MarketScreener). No failed auction or BOJ emergency operation reported.
plan_financing.rationale: Auctions are clearing well (BTC 3.76, well above rubric threshold of 3), ruling out a score of 2. However, 10y yields are at 30-year highs on persistent fiscal concern and the full funding path for Takaichi's stimulus programme remains credibly unspecified per market analysts, satisfying the rubric's UNCLEAR condition of 'funding path unspecified OR yield up >25bps on fiscal news but auctions still clearing.'

dissent.view: Finobird/TradingEconomics characterise the higher auction yield (3.101% vs prior 2.995%) as signalling 'softer investor demand,' implying more stress than the strong BTC ratio suggests

MUFG Research forecast range of 2.90-3.30% for 10y JGB and notes concerns about BOJ falling behind the curve as main driver, not a discrete fiscal shock, suggesting gradual drift rather than UNCLEAR event

direct_lending_default.fact: Fitch Ratings reported the trailing 12-month US private credit default rate (across ~1,300 borrowers, inclusive of distressed exchanges and liability-management exercises) rose to a record 6.3% at end-August 2026, up from 6.1% in July; Fitch also recorded the highest monthly default event total in the prior 12 months (14 events in August). Source: Bloomberg citing Fitch Ratings report, September 14 2026 (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/us-private-credit-default-rate-hits-a-record-of-6-3-fitch-says); corroborated by Investment Executive, September 14 2026 (https://www.investmentexecutive.com/news/research-and-markets/u-s-private-credit-defaults-rise-fitch-4/).
direct_lending_default.rationale: The 6.3% Fitch TTM print (August 2026) is the load-bearing fact under the rubric: it uses Fitch's broad definition inclusive of distressed exchanges and maturity extensions, is a fresh record above the April 2026 prior record of 6.0%, and no newer Fitch monthly print is publicly available as of 2026-10-12. The escalating trajectory — 5.7% Q1 → 6.0% Q2/April-May → 6.1% July → 6.3% August — corroborates sustained and worsening funding stress in private credit, consistent with elevated PIK-loan reliance and dealer-balance-sheet sensitivity to middle-market credit deterioration.

dissent.view: Proskauer Private Credit Default Index: 2.51% for Q2 2026 (counts payment and financial-covenant defaults only, excludes maturity extensions)
KBRA Middle Market Default Monitor by count: 3.3% for twelve months to 30 June 2026 (adds imminent defaults and interventions)
KBRA Middle Market Default Monitor by debt: 2.4% for twelve months to 30 June 2026 (dollar-weighted)
Moody's private credit estimate: 1.6%-4.7% range for full-year 2025 (range depends on whether distressed exchanges are counted)

redemption_gates.fact: Per Valuation Research (Oct 2, 2026), average redemption requests across 11 of the 14 largest non-traded BDCs stood at 13.0% in Q3 2026, still well above the standard 5% quarterly cap, with named funds including Blackstone BCRED (~$79B, gated at 5% after ~10% requests per Yardeni/Bloomberg Sept 2026), Cliffwater Corporate Lending Fund (~$31B, capped at 5% after 16% requests), and Blue Owl OTIC/funds (capped at 5%, 39% requests) all actively gating in Q3; in Q2 2026 Fitch tracked 10 of 16 BDCs breaching caps on $15.6B in requests (Fitch/angelinvestorsnetwork.com, ~Aug 2026); cumulative gated AUM across BCRED, Apollo ADS, BlackRock HLEND, Ares ASIF, Cliffwater, Partners Group, Blue Owl funds exceeds $250B.
redemption_gates.rationale: The rubric threshold for WIDESPREAD is >=3 of the largest funds gating in the same quarter or combined AUM >$100B; at least 7-10 named major funds have simultaneously breached their 5% quarterly repurchase caps across Q1-Q3 2026 with combined AUM well exceeding $250B, satisfying the WIDESPREAD criterion by a large margin. Corroborating signals include: FOMC policy anchored at 3.50-3.75% (higher-for-longer), sticky CPI at 4.2%, new direct-lending issuance down ~40%, and a $14B cumulative redemption backlog reported by Bloomberg (July 2026), all consistent with structural funding stress in semi-liquid private credit vehicles.

new_imf_programs.fact: IMF FY2026 Annual Report (May 2025-Apr 2026) records only 2 new nonprecautionary Board-approved arrangements for the full fiscal year; IMF homepage (Oct 7 2026) shows latest action is a Staff-Monitored Program with Yemen (not a lending arrangement); BoC-BoE Sovereign Default Database 2026 edition notes sovereign debt in default fell 14% in 2025 and no new missed coupons are reported in the trailing 6-month window; MacKay Shields Aug 2026 notes 'the cluster of sovereign crisis between 2020 and 2023 is largely behind us' with Zambia, Ghana and Sri Lanka having restructured; staff-level ECF agreements with Senegal and Guinea are pipeline items not yet Board-approved.
new_imf_programs.rationale: Zero Board-approved new IMF nonprecautionary lending arrangements and zero missed coupons or defaults are confirmed in the Apr-Oct 2026 window; pipeline staff-level agreements (Senegal, Guinea) and the Yemen SMP are 'talk' not 'action' under the rubric, so the count is 0, mapping to CALM.

dissent.view: Senegal ECF and Guinea ECF staff-level agreements, plus Bangladesh new programme negotiations, could be counted as early-stage distress signals by some analysts, pushing toward RISING if Board approval comes through in Q4 2026

china_ppi.fact: China PPI rose +3.8% year-on-year in August 2026, per NBS release dated 9 September 2026 (landedmath.com citing NBS; corroborated by admiralmarkets.com preview table and investing.com calendar). September 2026 data is not yet published; NBS release scheduled 14 October 2026.
china_ppi.rationale: The rubric requires the signed YoY percent as published by NBS; +3.8% is the latest confirmed official figure. The engine scores on magnitude: +3.8% is a moderately elevated positive reading, signalling cost-push pressure at factory gates that could export input-cost inflation to trading partners.

trade_actions.fact: At least 6 distinct new major-economy trade measures against Chinese exports were enacted in the trailing 3 months: (1) EU definitive anti-dumping on Chinese car/lorry tyres (4.3%-45.3%), published July 7, 2026 (policy.trade.ec.europa.eu); (2) EU definitive anti-dumping on Chinese polyamide filament yarns (60%-67.6%), EU Reg. 2026/1823, July 27, 2026 (catts.eu/august-2026); (3) EU provisional anti-dumping on Chinese benzyl alcohol, July 27, 2026 (catts.eu/august-2026); (4) Canada CBSA provisional anti-dumping/CVD on unarmored building cables from China, effective July 29, 2026 (catts.eu/august-2026); (5) China extended anti-dumping on single-mode optical fiber from India, effective August 14, 2026 (catts.eu/august-2026); (6) US imposed 7.5% overcapacity tariff on China restoring ~20% total rate, reported August 24, 2026 (china-briefing.com). Simultaneously, the US-China bilateral truce was extended two months on September 27, 2026 (rvia.org), and US-China recommended $30bn in mutual tariff cuts (euronews.com, September 28, 2026). EU safeguard tariffs on Chinese hybrid EVs are under active deliberation but not yet enacted (asiatimes.com, October 9, 2026).
trade_actions.rationale: Six or more new measures in the trailing 3 months satisfies the rubric threshold of >=4 new measures for ESCALATING (score 2), and the EU tyre anti-dumping (up to 45.3%) qualifies as a broad tariff round exceeding 10% across a sector. The ongoing US-China truce extension prevents a clean 'truce breakdown' characterization, but the measure count and sectoral breadth independently clear the ESCALATING bar.

license_flow.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 18 (April 2025) — covering seven heavy/medium rare earths and derivative magnets including NdFeB and SmCo — remains fully in force and has never been suspended. General licenses exist but are limited to three named Chinese producers (JL MAG, Zhongke Sanhuan, Ningbo Yunsheng) covering only pre-vetted named customers. Per-shipment case-by-case review applies to all others, with a statutory 45-working-day target routinely exceeded at 60–120+ days in practice. In June 2026 MOFCOM added 10 US entities including MP Materials to its export-control list. Sources: cmgm.net (2026-08), blog.gettransport.com (2026-07), techtimes.com (2026-10-06), bisi.org.uk (2026-10-01).
license_flow.rationale: The regime meets Rubric Level 1 on three independent grounds: (a) general licences cover only a whitelist of three named producers and their pre-cleared customers, not most export volume; (b) typical processing exceeds 30 days (60–120+ days in practice); and (c) new categories were added within the trailing 3 months (US entity-list additions including rare-earth supply-chain players in June 2026). Level 2 is not warranted because licences are actively being issued and no categorical suspension or country-wide denial is in effect.

dissent.view: BISI (Oct 2026) reports that the one-year suspension of October 2025 controls has been extended to 10 January 2027 following a Trump-Xi Washington summit, suggesting a modest easing on the extraterritorial track; however, the core April 2025 licensing regime remains unaffected by this extension.

CFR (Oct 2026) characterises China as continuing to 'squeeze supply' throughout 2026 under earlier controls, and notes Beijing never publicly announced it would suspend or remove the April 2025 measures — implying effective tightness closer to a Level 2 read in practice, though no formal suspension of licensing has been declared.

truce_status.fact: US Treasury Secretary Bessent announced on Sep 23, 2026 an extension of the Busan truce from Nov 10, 2026 to Jan 10, 2027 (Investing.com/NBC News, Sep 23 2026); however, China added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export control entity list on Jun 22, 2026 (The Conversation/Modern Diplomacy), and US officials assessed Chinese rare-earth compliance at ~two-thirds of commitments with yttrium exports down ~95% (startupfortune.com, Oct 10 2026).
truce_status.rationale: The truce is formally extended (not lapsed), ruling out Score 2; but partial breaches — new entity-list additions targeting the two lead US rare-earth firms and persistent sub-commitment supply volumes — satisfy the rubric's 'partial breach' prong for Score 1 (EXPIRING/fraying), and the extended deadline of Jan 10 2027 is itself <90 days from today with no further renewal announced.

dissent.view: Some sources (startupfortune.com, Oct 6 2026) framed the Nov 10 date as expiring 'with no renewal in sight' before the Sep 23 extension was announced; post-extension reporting broadly converges on Jan 10 2027 as the new deadline, so the 'no renewal' characterisation is outdated but circulates in older articles.

re_blacklist.fact: On 22 June 2026, China MOFCOM issued Announcement No. 23 of 2026, adding 10 US entities to its export control list; the two named US rare-earth producers are MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth Inc. The restriction bans Chinese exporters and all global parties from supplying Chinese-origin dual-use items to those specific firms. Source: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026, corroborated by Bloomberg (2026-06-22), Al Jazeera (2026-06-22), Benchmark Minerals (2026-06-22), and Morgan Lewis (2026-07-01). Benchmark Minerals explicitly notes 'the measure is entity-specific rather than a blanket restriction on rare earth exports to the US.'
re_blacklist.rationale: Two named US rare-earth producers (MP Materials, USA Rare Earth) are on China's MOFCOM export-control list as of 22 June 2026, satisfying rubric level 1 (entity-specific). The restriction is firm-specific, not a categorical sector-wide or class ban on all US rare-earth producers, so level 2 is not warranted.

hree_premium.fact: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence Q3 2026 Rare Earths Price Review (published ~25 Sep 2026): 'CIF Europe dysprosium oxide prices are now around 16.3 times DDP China price levels, up from 6.8 times at the end of Q2.' BMI also records dysprosium oxide CIF Europe surging 150% over Q3.
hree_premium.rationale: The BMI 16.3× figure is a directly published price-ratio from a primary commodity-pricing agency covering the most liquid HREE benchmark (Dy oxide), satisfying the rubric's request for an ex-China premium multiple of the China price. North American transaction data (S&P Global: $3,250/kg vs ~$214/kg China = ~15×) independently corroborates the ~15-16× order of magnitude at Q3-end.

dissent.view: Indicative non-transaction ex-China Dy oxide prices (USA Rare Earth investor materials, Serra Verde contractual floor $575/kg) imply only a ~2.7-5× premium, far below cleared-transaction multiples; these are contractual floors or broker indications, not spot transactions.
Price-Watch.ai characterises Q3 2026 Dy market as 'mildly bearish' globally, implying limited ex-China premium — but this tracks China FOB prices, not the ex-China scarcity premium.
REEx Oct 2 2026 reports a wide range of 3-17× for dysprosium ex-China premium, depending on transaction type, volume and qualification status.

genius_impl.fact: The GENIUS Act Section 13 rulemaking deadline of July 18, 2026 passed with zero final rules published by any primary federal regulator (OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC, NCUA, Treasury/FinCEN/OFAC). As of October 2, 2026, 13+ NPRMs and one interim final rule had been issued but none finalized; the Federal Reserve only issued its NPRM on September 24, 2026 with comments open until November 30, 2026; the OCC is targeting a final rule by November 2026. Sources: regwatch.io tracker (2 Oct 2026), federalregister.gov 2026-19860 (Fed NPRM, 29 Sep 2026), frame.xyz/insights/genius-act-final-rules (18 Jul 2026), Freshfields (25 Aug 2026), PYMNTS (20 Aug 2026).
genius_impl.rationale: The rubric scores 2 = PROBLEMS when the deadline is missed without final rules; every primary regulator missed the July 18, 2026 statutory deadline and no final implementing rule has been published as of the research date, satisfying the rubric condition unambiguously. There is no court stay or compliance-failure event, but the plain deadline miss with zero finalized rules is sufficient for a 2 rating.

dissent.view: Paradigm GENIUS Act Rulemaking Tracker shows '0/25 Final Rule completed' as of ~Oct 2026, consistent with a deadline miss but frames agency misses as common and without formal penalty, implying limited systemic consequence.

toku.com (4 Aug 2026) characterizes the miss as 'not a scandal and not unusual' given multi-agency coordination complexity, suggesting the practical impact is mitigated by the January 2027 effective date backstop.

ai_revenue_gap.fact: Combined hyperscaler 2026 capex guided ~$725B, up ~77% YoY (vs ~$410B in 2025); Microsoft FY26Q3 capex $30.9B–$34.9B up ~85% YoY with AI revenue run rate $37B +123% YoY; Google Cloud Q2 2026 +82% YoY; AWS Q2 2026 +37% YoY (fastest in 18 quarters); Amazon raised 2026 capex to ~$220B; Alphabet to $195–205B; Microsoft to ~$190B. Sources: Microsoft FY26 Q3 press release (Apr 29 2026, microsoft.com/investor), tech-insider.org Oct 11 2026, earningsshot.com Jul 2026.
ai_revenue_gap.rationale: Capex growth (~77–100% YoY aggregate) materially exceeds AI-attributable cloud revenue growth (~37–82% YoY), placing the gap firmly 'WIDE'; however, AI revenue is still strongly accelerating YoY across all four hyperscalers with no guidance cuts, so rubric score 1 applies rather than 2.

dissent.view: Some analysts argue the gap is effectively 'closing' for AWS specifically, citing AI at a $25B+ run rate growing triple digits and AWS margin expansion to above pre-AI-cycle levels, suggesting returns are arriving faster than feared.
Meta's FCF collapsed (only $12B against $145B capex plan) and markets punished Meta ~6% for raising capex without proportional revenue proof, suggesting for Meta the dynamic may be closer to score 2.

gpu_refi_stress.fact: JPMorgan, MUFG and co-lenders have spent 6+ months failing to fully distribute $38B in Oracle-leased data center construction debt (Texas/Wisconsin); some banks are now selling pieces at a discount to non-bank buyers. S&P cut Oracle to BBB- in July 2026; Oracle 5-yr CDS ~151 bps in early Oct 2026 (widest since 2009). Separately, ~$18B in Oracle-leased New Mexico loans quoted at 89-91 cents. No confirmed default or distressed exchange reported. Sources: Bloomberg/FT cited by Startup Fortune (Oct 11 2026), Archynewsy (Oct 11 2026), DisruptionBanking (Sep 24 2026).
gpu_refi_stress.rationale: Banks offloading AI/data-center debt at a discount and Oracle facing a sustained $38B syndication wall — with an S&P downgrade to BBB- and CDS at 15-year wides — squarely satisfies Rubric-1 ('banks offloading AI/data-center debt at a discount, a named borrower facing a refinancing wall, or a rating watch on GPU-backed paper'). No confirmed default or distressed exchange has been reported, precluding Rubric-2.

dissent.view: Moody's awarded its first-ever Aaa to a data center securitization (Compass Datacenters, $830M, Feb 2026), and CoreWeave closed an $8.5B investment-grade GPU-backed facility in Q2 2026, suggesting the rated/hyperscaler tier is still accessing markets normally.

DisruptionBanking (Sep 24 2026) concludes 'no evidence of such a cascade exists today' and characterises conditions as 'a vulnerability rather than a systemic event', with Chicago Fed estimating direct AI-adjacent bank exposure at only ~0.8% of total assets.

cmbs_office_delinq.fact: Trepp September 2026 CMBS office delinquency rate: 12.16%, up 16 bps from August's 12.00%; per vaquerowealth.com (Oct 6 2026) and curatedcommercial.substack.com (Oct 12 2026), both citing Trepp September 2026 data.
cmbs_office_delinq.rationale: The Trepp September 2026 office CMBS delinquency rate of 12.16% is the most recent published figure and maps directly to the rubric, which calls for the latest percent reading from Trepp; this sits near cycle highs and reflects persistent maturity-default stress in the office sector.

dissent.view: KBRA reports a higher office CMBS delinquency rate of ~12.8% (Feb-Mar 2026) due to inclusion of a broader KBRA-rated universe and different loan classification methodology

regional_bank_stress.fact: FDIC failed-bank list shows 5 US bank failures in the trailing 6 months (Apr 12-Oct 12 2026): Community Bank and Trust-West Georgia (May 1), Kentland Federal S&L (Jul 10), Small Business Bank (Jul 17), Tioga-Franklin Savings Bank (Aug 21), and Nano Banc (Sep 25, $736M assets). Of these, Nano Banc is explicitly CRE-linked: American Banker (Sep 26 2026) reports it 'had been the subject of enforcement actions in connection with both commercial real estate lending and governance issues'; FedFis notes 'high concentrations in CRE'; a March 2026 DFPI consent order cited deteriorating financial condition tied to CRE concentration. Metropolitan Capital (Jan 30, CRE skilled-nursing loan) falls outside the 6-month window. No other in-window failure has explicit primary-source CRE attribution. No single failure exceeded $10bn assets; no coordinated interagency CRE supervisory action found. Source: fdic.gov/bank-failures/failed-bank-list (Oct 2026); americanbanker.com (Sep 28 2026); fintechcowboys.com/bank-failure-alert-nano-banc.
regional_bank_stress.rationale: Within the trailing 6 months, at least 1 confirmed CRE-linked failure (Nano Banc, $736M assets, <$10bn) with a public enforcement action explicitly citing CRE concentration satisfies the ISOLATED threshold of 1-2 such failures each <$10bn plus >=1 new enforcement action/consent order citing CRE concentration. CLUSTER (2) is not warranted because credible sources do not firmly attribute >=3 in-window failures primarily to CRE exposure, and no single failure exceeded $10bn or triggered a coordinated interagency action.

govt_stability.fact: The Second Lecornu government (formed 10 Oct 2025) is the incumbent minority government of France. It has survived multiple no-confidence votes (most recently 2 Feb 2026, when two motions fell short of the 289-vote threshold), invoked Article 49.3 repeatedly to pass the 2026 budget, and PM Lecornu remains in office as of 9-10 Oct 2026. Sources: Wikipedia 'Second Lecornu government'; Euronews 02 Feb 2026; Al Jazeera 02 Feb 2026; JPost 09 Oct 2026.
govt_stability.rationale: France operates under a hung parliament with an explicit minority-coalition status; the government has governed only by deploying Art. 49.3 and surviving successive no-confidence votes without ever holding a working majority — the textbook definition of rubric band 1 (FRAGILE). No collapse, resignation, or dissolution has occurred.

rating_action.fact: S&P downgraded France from AA- to A+ on 18 Oct 2025 (within trailing 12 months); Fitch had cut AA- to A+ on 12 Sep 2025; Moody's affirmed Aa3 but moved outlook to Negative on 24 Oct 2025, reaffirmed 10 Apr 2026. Current ratings per AFT (aft.gouv.fr, accessed Oct 2026): Fitch A+/Stable (28 Aug 2026), S&P A+/Stable (29 May 2026), Moody's Aa3/Negative (10 Apr 2026).
rating_action.rationale: S&P executed an actual one-notch rating cut (AA- to A+) on 18 Oct 2025, which falls inside the trailing 12-month window ending 12 Oct 2026, satisfying rubric band 2 (downgrade). Moody's negative outlook also independently satisfies band 1, but the S&P cut is the most severe signal and triggers band 2.

dissent.view: Fitch and S&P both show Stable outlooks at their most recent reviews (Aug and May 2026 respectively), suggesting no further deterioration post-cut — one could argue current posture is band 1 if trailing-12M window is read narrowly to exclude the Oct 2025 cuts

subprime_auto_dpd.fact: Fitch Auto ABS subprime 60+ day delinquency index reversed course to 6.13% in July 2026, up from 5.80% in June 2026, per cucollector.com citing Fitch data (published ~Sept 2026). The January 2026 record was 6.90%; the index fell through mid-year on tax-refund seasonality before rebounding in July.
subprime_auto_dpd.rationale: The rubric requires the latest reported Fitch subprime ABS 60+ day delinquency percent; July 2026 at 6.13% is the most recent monthly Fitch index figure surfaced, consistent with the documented seasonal second-half deterioration pattern. This is an ABS-pool measure of securitized subprime collateral, not the full auto loan universe, but is the standard industry benchmark for the indicator.

dissent.view: IBISWorld cites Fitch June 2026 subprime 60-day delinquency at 5.67%, vs. 5.80% cited by cucollector.com for the same month from Fitch—minor discrepancy likely reflecting index revision or rounding
ankso.blog cites Fitch data showing the rate eased to 5.49% by May 2026 (lowest since May 2024), consistent directionally but not the latest figure

bnpl_delinq.fact: Affirm Q4 FY2026 Earnings Supplement (Aug 27, 2026): 30+ DPD on monthly installment loans ex-Peloton/Pay-in-X = 2.5%, down from 2.7-2.8% in prior three quarters but up ~29 bps YoY in FQ3'26 per shareholder letter; cohort net charge-offs track ~3.5% of GMV (lifetime vintage). CFPB Dec-2025 report: aggregate BNPL pay-in-four charge-off rate 1.83% in 2023 (latest official figure). Richmond Fed Feb-2026: 'no direct evidence of rising aggregate BNPL charge-off rates to date.'
bnpl_delinq.rationale: 30+ DPD rose ~18-29 bps YoY through mid-FY2026 before improving in Q4, placing it squarely in the RISING band; the <100 bps YoY move precludes Score 2, and charge-offs remain below 3% on the regulator's pay-in-four series and below 5% on Affirm's own vintage metric, consistent with Score 1.

dollar_reserve_share.fact: IMF COFER data brief published 30 September 2026 (data.imf.org): 'the dollar\'s share of global foreign exchange reserves declined to 56.70 percent' in 2026Q2, from 57.18 percent in 2026Q1. Total global FX reserves rose to $13.22 trillion. Source: https://data.imf.org/en/news/imf%20data%20brief%20september%2030
dollar_reserve_share.rationale: The IMF COFER release dated 30-Sep-2026 is the most recent official publication; it reports 56.70% as the USD share for end-June 2026 (2026Q2), which maps directly and mechanically to the rubric requiring the latest published percent figure.

weaponization_event.fact: The 18th BRICS Summit (New Delhi, 12-13 Sep 2026) adopted the New Delhi Declaration formally endorsing BRICS Pay and local-currency settlement interoperability, but per Fair Observer post-summit analysis (c. 10 Oct 2026): 'the final declaration confined itself to promoting the interlinking of national payment systems and trade in local currencies, with no formal launch announced.' No new sovereign reserve freeze or seizure has been executed in 2026; the EU permanent-seizure proposal for ~EUR 210bn in Russian assets remains in deliberation. (Sources: Fair Observer Oct 2026; Wikipedia 18th BRICS Summit; Brookings/CFR on Russian assets)
weaponization_event.rationale: BRICS Pay received multilateral political endorsement and the New Delhi Declaration commits members to non-dollar settlement, qualifying as 'new non-dollar settlement agreements/launches or official rhetoric' under band 1; however, no operational live launch occurred and no new sovereign reserve was seized, so band 2 is not met.

dissent.view: Several non-primary outlets (informedclearly.com, economy.com.pk) assert BRICS Pay 'began operational deployment in 2026' with intra-bloc local-currency trade at 67%, which if accurate could shade toward band 2; however these sources lack official or wire-service corroboration and conflict with Fair Observer's post-summit finding of no formal launch.

insurer_exits.fact: Foster (2026) documented elevated nonrenewal rates in 13 states (many Midwest + CA/FL/LA); Weiss Ratings (Sep 8, 2026) named Utah the new nonrenewal epicenter at 4.45% of policies, ahead of CA (2.93%) and FL. NAIC 2026 Spring Meeting data call confirmed nonrenewal rates up 96%-216% across all four U.S. regions (NAIC/CNBC Aug 2026). No top-10 insurer fully exited a major state in 2026: State Farm CA rate settlement finalized Jul 23 2026 with no new block non-renewals; Allstate filed to return to CA Sep 1 2026; FL Citizens shrank from 1.42M to ~266K policies. Sources: RFF/Foster 2026 (rff.org); Weiss Ratings via advorahq.com Jun 2026; NAIC data call content.naic.org Mar 2026; CNBC Aug 6 2026.
insurer_exits.rationale: At least 13 states show active non-renewal waves, placing the count squarely in the 5-15 range of the RISING tier; however, major markets like FL and CA are showing partial stabilization (Citizens depopulation, State Farm settlement, Allstate re-entry filing), and no top-10 insurer has executed a full state exit in 2026, precluding the ACCELERATING (level 2) classification.

dissent.view: Some markets characterize the situation as still accelerating given the NAIC finding that nonrenewal rates climbed up to 216% across all regions and the California moratorium expiring in Jan 2026 triggering new non-renewals in LA/Palisades ZIP codes (latentinsure.com, May 2026)

cat_losses.fact: H1 2026 global insured nat-cat losses: USD 42bn (Swiss Re Institute, Aug 11 2026), 16% below the 10-year average of ~USD 50bn for H1; Munich Re confirms USD 44bn vs 10-yr avg of USD 50bn (Jul 30 2026); Aon estimates USD 47bn (H1 2026 recap). Hurricane Isaias (first hurricane of season, Cat 3 at peak) made landfall ~Oct 9-10 with pre-landfall insured loss estimates of USD 4-6bn (BMS/Gallagher Re, Oct 9 2026, theinsurer.com), explicitly below USD 10bn. No single 2026 event has exceeded USD 10bn insured. YTD total remains below the 10-year average.
cat_losses.rationale: YTD insured losses are below the 10-year average through H1 and the only hurricane of the season (Isaias) is tracking to sub-$10bn insured losses; both conditions required for NORMAL (0) are met - YTD <= 10y average and no single event >$10bn.

dissent.view: Aon H1 2026 estimate of $47bn is slightly above the 21st-century H1 average per Aon's own framing ('slightly above the 21st-century average'), though still below Munich Re's 10-year H1 average of $50bn and Swiss Re's trend of $66bn

ss_reform_news.fact: The 2026 SSA Trustees Report (released June 9, 2026) projects the OASI trust fund depleted Q4 2032 (one quarter earlier than the 2025 report), and the combined OASDI funds depleted Q3 2034 (unchanged). Long-term funding gap widened to 4.42% of taxable payroll. Multiple reform bills introduced (H.R. 9187 Bipartisan Social Security Commission Act; S 4979 PROMISE Act) but none enacted. No automatic benefit cut has been triggered. Sources: SSA 2026 Trustees Report (ssa.gov/oact/); CRS IF13256; CRFB.org (July 16 2026); BPC (June 9 2026).
ss_reform_news.rationale: The trustees report worsened the OASI depletion date by one quarter and meaningfully enlarged the long-term deficit, and reform legislation is actively debated in Congress -- satisfying rubric band 1. No cut has been legislated or automatically triggered, so band 2 is not met.

dissent.view: AARP and Key.com characterise the combined OASDI depletion date as unchanged at 2034, framing the report as 'largely unchanged'; BPC/CRFB/401kSpecialist emphasise the OASI-only fund moved to 2032 (one year earlier), a meaningful deterioration driven by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

pension_leverage_event.fact: Bank of England FPC Record – March 2026 (published 1 April 2026) states: 'The FPC noted that the liability driven investment (LDI) sector had remained resilient in the current market environment,' supported by post-2022 liquidity buffer requirements (min 250 bps TPR/300 bps ESMA). The July 2026 BoE Financial Stability Report (data as at 25 June 2026) confirmed 'The LDI sector also remained resilient, reflecting policy measures taken since the Autumn 2022 gilt market stress.' The September 2026 FPC Record (meeting 25 September 2026) makes no mention of any LDI stress episode. A March 2026 gilt selloff produced only 'limited pension cash calls' and 'far smaller' impact than 2022 per Reuters/AlphaSquawk (August 2026 update), with the PPF Purple Book 2025 aggregate DB funding ratio at 125% and a net surplus of £214bn. Sources: bankofengland.co.uk FPC Records March/July/September 2026; BoE FSR July 2026; alphasquawk.com August 2026.
pension_leverage_event.rationale: Multiple FPC records through September 2026 explicitly characterise the LDI sector as resilient with adequate buffers; the March 2026 gilt selloff produced only limited, manageable cash calls and no forced selling or central-bank intervention. This maps cleanly to rubric band 0 (buffers adequate, no margin stress).

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman 100 Public Pension Funding Index (PPFI) funded ratio: 88.2% as of July 31, 2026, covering the 100 largest U.S. public defined benefit plans. Source: Milliman PPFI August 2026 update (published August 27, 2026), https://www.milliman.com/en/insight/public-pension-funding-index-august-2026
funded_ratio.rationale: The Milliman PPFI is the standard monthly tracker for the 100 largest U.S. public pensions; 88.2% maps directly to the rubric as the representative funded ratio. Equable Institute's broader 253-plan universe yields 85.0% for FY2026, a materially different reading recorded in dissent.

dissent.view: Equable Institute 'State of Pensions 2026' reports 85.0% national average funded ratio for U.S. state and local pension plans as of June 30, 2026, covering 253 statewide and municipal systems — the highest since 2009 but $1.13 trillion short of full funding.

interconnection_months.fact: LBNL Queued Up: 2026 Edition (data workbook updated May 2026, PDF June 2026, emp.lbl.gov/queues): median IR-to-COD for projects reaching commercial operation in 2025 was 61 months (~5.1 years), down from 63 months for the 2024 in-service cohort.
interconnection_months.rationale: The load-bearing figure is the 61-month median from interconnection request to commercial operation for the 2025 in-service cohort (n=294, LBNL sheet 37), the most current published LBNL datapoint; this maps directly to the rubric requesting 'latest median grid interconnection wait in months'.

dissent.view: LBNL Queued Up 2025 Edition (data through end-2024) reported 55 months median IR-to-COD for the 2024 in-service cohort; Loopback Systems and other secondary sources citing this older edition still quote 55 months.
LBNL 2026 Edition narrative states 'well over 3 years' for IR-to-IA (not full IR-to-COD), which is a partial-stage metric not comparable to the full 61-month figure.

dc_moratoria.fact: New York Governor Hochul signed Executive Order No. 62 on July 14, 2026, imposing the first enacted statewide data center moratorium in the U.S. (pausing DEC permits for facilities ≥50 MW). Additionally, DLA Piper (July 2026) reported 'more than 100 local moratoria have been adopted nationwide,' with confirmed enacted pauses in Baltimore MD (June 16), Snohomish County WA (June 24), St. Charles MO (May 19 permanent ban), Lysander NY (May 7), Austin County TX, and multiple Indiana counties, among others. Sources: davispolk.com (July 23, 2026); dlapiper.com (July 1, 2026); dcmap.us (Oct 2026).
dc_moratoria.rationale: Rubric level 2 requires a statewide moratorium enacted OR >10 jurisdictions with enacted pauses: New York's EO 62 (July 14, 2026) is a confirmed enacted statewide moratorium, and corroborating sources document well over 10 additional local enacted pauses across multiple states, satisfying both prongs of the top band.

dissent.view: electricchoice.com (Oct 2026) claims '482 moratoria currently in force across 44 states' — a figure far higher than other trackers and likely includes proposed/pending actions or very minor local ordinances, not just enacted construction pauses

ai_power_pressure.fact: The U.S. DOE invoked Section 202(c) of the Federal Power Act at least three times in 2026 to curtail data-center loads on PJM and ERCOT: (1) ERCOT emergency order 202-26-01 issued Jan 24 2026 (DOE.gov); (2) PJM emergency order issued May 18 2026 (Utility Dive, May 19 2026); (3) two PJM emergency orders in effect July 1-3 2026 during a record 168,158 MW peak, forcing data centers >=50 MW onto diesel backup within 15 minutes (electricchoice.com / techtimes.com, July 4 2026). In parallel, New York passed a statewide data-center moratorium (July 2026) and Texas halted new data-center permits pending an energy audit (Sept 2026), per environmentamerica.org.
ai_power_pressure.rationale: Confirmed curtailment of data-center load under declared federal grid emergencies satisfies the rubric's Level 2 threshold exactly; multiple separate DOE 202(c) orders on both PJM and ERCOT constitute confirmed forced curtailment and declared grid emergencies, not merely warnings or forecasts. State-level power-scarcity-driven moratoria (NY, TX) add further corroboration.

dissent.view: Some sources frame 2026 conditions as severe queue congestion and project delays (Level 1 territory) without referencing the emergency curtailment orders, focusing on the 2,600 GW national interconnection backlog and 5-12 year wait times as the primary story.

IEA Electricity 2026 report characterises the situation as projects 'stalled in connection queues worldwide' and a need to raise grid investment by 50% by 2030 -- framing that implies structural tightness rather than active curtailment events.

mine_disruptions.fact: Three confirmed major-mine disruptions active simultaneously: (1) Grasberg Block Cave (world #2) running at ~60% of capacity during phased ramp-up following Sep 2025 mud rush, with 2026 output ~35% below pre-incident forecast per Freeport 10-Q filed 2026; (2) Kamoa-Kakula (top-5 globally) 2026 guidance cut from 420,000 t to 290,000-330,000 t after 2025 seismic/flood event plus a 56-day smelter shutdown in Q2 2026 (mining.com, April 1 2026; Ivanhoe Q2 2026 release); (3) Antofagasta Centinela strike by 709 workers since Oct 7 2026, mining/haulage/development disrupted with unions projecting ~50% output cut in November (northernminer.com, discoveryalert.com, Oct 8-12 2026). BMI revised 2026 copper deficit from 72,000 t to 400,000 t citing these disruptions; Cochilco forecasts 5.27 Mt Chilean output, lowest since 2003 (discoveryalert.com, Oct 12 2026).
mine_disruptions.rationale: Three named top-20 mines (Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula, Centinela) have confirmed, physically measured production cuts currently active, satisfying the >=3 threshold; additionally, multiple institutions (Goldman Sachs, BMI) have explicitly forecast a market deficit attributable to these combined losses, satisfying both prongs of the rubric's level-2 definition.

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG April 2026 Copper Market Forecast revised the 2026 refined copper balance to a surplus of approximately 96,000 tonnes, reversing its October 2025 projection of a 150,000-tonne deficit; source: ICSG via MarketScreener/IndexBox/MiningWeekly, dated 23 April 2026.
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: A forecast surplus of +96,000t sits just outside the +/-100kt balanced band on the surplus side, mapping to rubric band 0 (SURPLUS). Confidence is medium because the margin is narrow — only ~4kt beyond the balanced threshold — and ICSG's own July 2026 monthly data showed a 51,000-tonne deficit, suggesting the full-year balance remains highly uncertain.

dissent.view: ICSG preliminary monthly data showed a 51,000-tonne refined copper deficit for July 2026, suggesting the actual year-to-date trajectory may be tightening relative to the April full-year surplus forecast.

ICSG Jan-May 2026 preliminary data showed a 221,000-tonne apparent surplus (189,000t adjusted), well above the April full-year forecast of 96,000t surplus, pointing to a wider surplus than the annual projection.

drought_chip_farm.fact: Taiwan's Water Resources Agency imposed formal water rationing after 'the driest winter in 75 years,' with reservoirs in chipmaking hub Hsinchu County at 60-80% of 2021 severe-drought levels and Zengwen Reservoir at 28.5% capacity; private industries cut usage up to 7%. Source: Taipei Times, 2026-03-27 (https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2026/03/27/2003854549). By Aug-Oct 2026 southern Taiwan reservoir levels improved with rainfall (Astute Group, ~Aug 2026), but TSMC CEO still cited water as a production-planning concern in June 2026.
drought_chip_farm.rationale: A confirmed government water-rationing order affecting chipmaking hubs Hsinchu and Taichung satisfies rubric level 2 ('confirmed production curtailment / water-rationing order at a fab'). The US Southwest concurrently improved to D0-D1 after tropical moisture (USDM Oct 8, 2026), so Taiwan is the binding region driving the score.

dissent.view: By ~August 2026, recent rainfall improved southern Taiwan reservoir levels, reducing immediate pressure on industrial water supplies — suggesting conditions may have retreated from acute to emerging by Q4 2026.

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation 1,037.7 ft, storage 6,820,887 acre-feet, 26.1% of USBR active capacity (26.12M AF basis) as of Oct 11, 2026 — a record low since the reservoir first filled; per U.S. Bureau of Reclamation daily gauge data via coloradorivermonitor.com (USBR feed). Minimum power pool is 950 ft; reservoir is ~87.7 ft above that threshold.
reservoir_stress.rationale: At 26.1% of capacity, Lake Mead is firmly below the rubric's 30% CRITICAL threshold, satisfying the level-2 criterion outright. The record-low elevation constitutes a confirmed physical impact (not merely a forecast), further anchoring the top-band classification.

dissent.view: lakelevelnow.com uses 28.95M AF total design capacity, yielding ~24% full — slightly lower percentage but same rubric band (CRITICAL).
reservoirbench.com cites 26,120,000 AF capacity basis and reports 26.1% full as of Oct 7, 2026 — consistent with primary reading.

water_dispute.fact: India placed the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in 'abeyance' on 23 April 2025 following the Pahalgam terror attack and continues to hold it so as of October 2026. On 31 August 2026, the Permanent Court of Arbitration (The Hague) ruled unanimously that the IWT remains fully in force and India's abeyance is legally impermissible; India rejected the ruling and the court's jurisdiction. Pakistan's Deputy PM raised the abeyance with the UN Secretary-General on 6 October 2026. No deliberate physical flow cut-off or armed clash has been documented. (Sources: pakera.pk, 11 Oct 2026; Al Jazeera, 1 Sep 2026; ISAS NUS, 28 Apr 2026)
water_dispute.rationale: The IWT is formally contested/suspended by one party (India) and rejected as such by the other (Pakistan), with active UN Security Council diplomacy and an international arbitral ruling — squarely a 'treaty suspended/contested with official threats exchanged' scenario. No kinetic action or confirmed physical diversion of water has been reported, so the threshold for level 2 is not met.

dissent.view: Egypt-Ethiopia/GERD dispute also rates TENSE: Egypt issued 'all necessary measures' language at the UN on 26 Sep 2026 and Ethiopia is advancing three new Blue Nile dams, but no armed clash or confirmed flow cut-off occurred, so it also maps to 1 rather than 2.

India's position frames the abeyance as a sovereign security act, not a treaty violation, which could be read as treaty-functioning-under-force-majeure rather than 'contested'; however, the PCA explicitly rejected this framing.

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 136.0 points in September 2026, up 2.0 points (+1.5%) MoM from revised August and +5.8% YoY; third consecutive monthly increase and highest since November 2022. Source: FAO (fao.org/newsroom), released 2 October 2026.
fao_food_trend.rationale: MoM rise of 1.5% is below the 5% SPIKING threshold and the 3-month gain (Jul-Sep) is ~3.7%, well below 10%; index is rising and at a post-2022 high, placing it squarely in ELEVATED (band 1).

china_export_curbs.fact: China's NDRC-linked phosphate export suspension (announced Dec 2025, extended March 2026 to cover additional phosphate varieties and NK blends) continues through at least end-2026; the 2026 urea export quota is set at 3.3 million tonnes with FOB price floors of $430-440/t -- a 34% cut vs 2025 actuals -- though Bloomberg (Aug 2026) reports the allowance was later revised up to ~5 Mt. Food Security Portal August 2026 update: 'phosphate stayed tight on constrained Sulphur supply and China's continuing export suspension.' (Sources: foodsecurityportal.org Aug 2026; S&P Global/Platts Dec 11 2025; fertilizerdaily.com Jul 29 2026; procurementinstitute.io; discoveryalert.com Sep 2026)
china_export_curbs.rationale: Active phosphate export suspension and urea volume quota with price floors are both confirmed in effect as of August-September 2026, squarely matching rubric level 1 (restrictions in place, unchanged). The last confirmed broadening occurred in March 2026, outside the trailing 3-month window from Oct 12 2026, so level 2 is not warranted.

dissent.view: Bloomberg (reported via agbull.com, Aug 27 2026) indicates China's 2026 urea export allowance was expanded to ~5.0-5.5 Mt, near 2025 levels, suggesting partial normalization on nitrogen -- though phosphate restrictions remain firm.

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on Oct 4 vs. pre-crisis baseline of 85/day; Brent at ~$103-104/bbl; Gulf sulfur shipments collapsed to 147,000 MT in June vs. 11-year floor of 730,000 MT; FAO reports 3-4 Mt/month of fertilizer trade stalled; strait effectively closed since Feb 28 2026 with ongoing vessel attacks and deadlocked negotiations (straits.live, IFPRI, FAO/openknowledge, Oct 12 2026)
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: The strait is rated CLOSED with throughput near zero (4 vs. 85 daily transits) and Brent above $100/bbl corroborates the closure signal; sulfur and ammonia fertilizer input flows from Gulf producers are effectively halted, satisfying both prongs of the rubric's level-2 threshold.

taiwan_tension.fact: China's Maritime Safety Administration issued no-sail notices for five sea areas (Bohai Sea, Yellow Sea, East China Sea, South China Sea) for PLA live-fire drills running 12-17 October 2026, following President Lai Ching-te's Double Ten National Day address. Taiwan's Defence Minister Wellington Koo assessed on 12 Oct that the exercises are held near China's coastline — not around Taiwan itself — and involve only PLA artillery units; 4 PLA aircraft sorties and 6 PLAN vessels were detected operating around Taiwan as of 06:00 local time. No kinetic clash or blockade was reported. Source: Taipei Times / Focus Taiwan / Reuters (via US News) / Hong Kong Free Press, 12 Oct 2026.
taiwan_tension.rationale: Active PLA live-fire drills across five maritime zones, framed as a coercive response to Taiwan's National Day speech, constitute assertive military activity well above routine — matching Rubric 1 (ELEVATED). However, drills are assessed by Taiwan's own MND as coastline-proximate artillery exercises with no encirclement of Taiwan, no blockade, and no kinetic clash, keeping the reading below Rubric 2 (CRISIS).

dissent.view: Democrata.es and some AFP wire aggregators characterise Koo's language as condemning 'reckless' exercises and Taiwan 'preparing for the worst', implying higher alarm — but Koo simultaneously assessed drills as far from Taiwan and limited to artillery units, undercutting a crisis-level read.
US East Asian envoy Michael DeSombre said on 9 Oct 2026 that investors are 'overpricing' Taiwan conflict risk, and that both sides want to avoid conflict — consistent with a below-crisis assessment.

export_controls.fact: Within the trailing 3 months (July–October 2026): (US/allied side) BIS June 1 2026 notice extended AI-chip licensing requirements to Chinese-company subsidiaries outside China; South Korea joined the Netherlands and Japan in licensing advanced chipmaking-equipment exports effective September 1 2026 (AsiaAI Chip Export Controls Tracker, updated ~Oct 1 2026); the MATCH Act (DUV blanket ban on ASML sales to China) remains before Congress. (China side) MOFCOM added 10 US entities to its Export Control List on June 22 2026, added 14 EU entities on July 24 2026 (including compound-semiconductor specialists III-V Lab and Vigo Photonics), enacted June 11 2026 tech-transfer rules granting explicit legal retaliation authority against nations restricting Chinese tech investments, and activated MOFCOM Announcement No. 26 on July 1 2026 formalising enforcement of strategic-mineral export controls — all confirmed by MOFCOM announcements, Morgan Lewis (July 1 2026), CFR (Sept 2026), and AsiaAI tracker (Oct 2026).
export_controls.rationale: Both sides have enacted new export-control measures in the trailing 3 months: the US/allied bloc tightened semiconductor-equipment licensing (South Korea join, June BIS guidance) and China enacted retaliatory entity-list additions targeting US and EU firms plus a new legal retaliation framework — satisfying rubric level 2 (target country countermeasures active). ASML-specific market signals corroborate the escalation: ASML China revenue fell from ~36% in Q4 2025 to ~19% in Q1 2026 per company disclosures.

dissent.view: East Asia Forum (March 2026) argued US controls 'have cooled down' and the Trump administration was downplaying chip controls to facilitate trade talks, implying a TIGHTENING rather than full RETALIATION dynamic; however subsequent June–July Chinese entity-list actions post-date this assessment.

fab_concentration.fact: As of Q3-Q4 2026, TSMC's entire <=3nm (N3 and N2) production capacity remains in Taiwan: N2 capacity ~90,000-120,000 wpm and N3 ~180,000 wpm are exclusively at Taiwan fabs (Hsinchu, Kaohsiung, Tainan). Arizona Fab 21 Phase 1 produces only N4/N5; Phase 2 (N3) began equipment installation in Q3 2026 with volume production targeted for 2H 2027. Japan JASM Kumamoto Fab 1 operates only mature nodes (6-28nm). No overseas fab is in volume production at <=3nm. Source: TSMC Q1 2026 earnings call (April 16 2026), TSMC investor page (tsmc.com/english/dedicatedFoundry/manufacturing/fab_capacity), TrendForce April 2026, Focus Taiwan April 2026, supply-chain sources via BigGoFinance September 2026.
fab_concentration.rationale: Zero operational overseas capacity at <=3nm nodes places the share outside Taiwan at effectively 0%, well below the <10% threshold for EXTREME. No operational overseas leading-edge fab exists at this node class, satisfying both conditions of rubric level 2.

dissent.view: A Phoenix city government release (July 2026) cited by tech-insider.org projects ~30% of 2nm-and-beyond capacity in Arizona 'once expanded fabs are complete' — a forward-looking estimate, not current operational capacity.

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 4 commercial vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz on Oct 4 2026 — roughly 5% of the pre-crisis baseline of ~85 per day — with war-risk insurance priced at 30x pre-crisis levels and Brent crude at ~$103-104/bbl (+44% vs pre-crisis ~$72). A top Iranian official on Oct 12 called the US response to its Hormuz reopening proposal 'inadequate', leaving no functioning diplomatic resolution in place. (Sources: straits.live live tracker 12 Oct 2026; IMF PortWatch Oct 4 2026; GulfNews/OilPrice.com Oct 12 2026)
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: Transit volume at 5% of normal (4 vessels/day vs ~85) is well under the 25% threshold; the closure is corroborated by Brent at ~$103-104/bbl (+44% above pre-crisis), satisfying the rubric's market-signal requirement for a '2' rating. No functioning convoy workaround or signed truce is in effect as of Oct 12, so the '1' cap condition does not apply.

dissent.view: Some dark/AIS-off tanker transits are occurring and Gulf crude exports recovered to ~81% of pre-war levels in September via alternative routes (East-West pipeline, Cape diversion), suggesting physical oil supply disruption is less severe than a hard closure implies.

CMA CGM resumed limited Red Sea transit with naval escort in 2026; some carriers use the Red Sea route opportunistically, indicating the Red Sea corridor itself is contested (1) rather than fully closed.

cable_incidents.fact: On 6 September 2025, at least four Red Sea cables (SMW4, IMEWE, FALCON GCX, Europe India Gateway) were severed near Jeddah by likely commercial anchor drag, causing internet degradation across India, Pakistan, Gulf states and Africa (Capacity Global / Gulf News, Sept 2025). PEACE and AAE-1 cuts from early 2025 were repaired by April 2025. No confirmed new Red Sea, Baltic, or Hormuz cut is reported in 2026; Iran issued credible Hormuz cable-cut threats (Asia Times, Sept 2026) and Baltic incidents remain under hybrid-warfare investigation but no unrepaired severance confirmed.
cable_incidents.rationale: The Sept 2025 Red Sea multi-cable cut is the most recent confirmed severing event but ~13 months elapsed and prior cuts of similar scale were repaired within weeks-to-months, so current severed status is unconfirmed; Iran Hormuz threats and ongoing Baltic hybrid-warfare pattern constitute credible ongoing threats, mapping to rubric level 1 (THREATENED) rather than 2 (CUT), as no market-corroborated unrepaired outage is confirmed for October 2026.

dissent.view: September 2025 Red Sea cuts to SMW4/IMEWE/FALCON/EIG may still be unrepaired given repair-ship scarcity and geopolitical permitting delays in Red Sea conflict zone
Iran threat to cut Hormuz cables assessed as operationally feasible and affecting project planning, implying elevated risk beyond mere threat

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: SIFMA/DTCC/BNY/Broadridge Pulse Survey (conducted June 2026, published Sept 22 2026): 86% of 340 respondents at least somewhat confident of meeting the mandate; however 45% still need more regulatory clarity, 88% of delayed programs cite legal/contract negotiation, and TBAC (May 2026) flagged two unresolved scoping issues (inter-affiliate exemptions, extraterritoriality) requiring pending SEC exemptive relief. No deadline extension issued; SEC reaffirmed Dec 31 2026 cash deadline (March 2026). Source: sifma.org press release Sept 22 2026; home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/TBACCharge1Q22026.pdf
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: Overall confidence (86%) clears the rubric 60% threshold and no deadline has been extended, ruling out score 2; but pending exemptive relief on inter-affiliate/extraterritorial scoping, widespread legal/documentation backlogs (88% of delayed firms), and 45% still lacking regulatory clarity squarely match the rubric definition of FRICTION (score 1). No corroborating SOFR-EFFR or repo spread stress prevents escalation to score 2.

dissent.view: DTCC FICC membership survey (Jul 27 2026) characterises industry as broadly ready for cash deadline with most firms 'already operationally ready' and >$1.2T daily already clearing, implying closer to score 0 for cash leg

ISDA/ICMA (Sept 2026) highlight that most cash Treasury market remains non-cleared and extraterritorial exemptive relief was still pending as of April 2026, suggesting friction closer to the upper end of score 1
